title: Lijiang Charges ¥50 to Enter. Dali's Old Town Is Free | China Travel Expert
description:
Lijiang asks a ¥50 old-town maintenance fee. Dali's old town, two hours south, charges nothing.

Dali sits in Yunnan beside Erhai Lake, under the Cangshan range. It's been a capital here for more than 1,200 years — the seat of the Nanzhao Kingdom from 738 CE, with the old-town walls rebuilt under the Ming in 1382. You walk straight in: no gate, no ticket. Lijiang, about two hours north, levies a ¥50 maintenance fee (valid 365 days) under rules effective August 2025. Same kind of cobbled lanes, Bai-style courtyard houses and snow-peak backdrop — one just doesn't charge you to see it.

🧭 Expert Tip: base yourself in Dali for the free, slower old town, and day-trip Lijiang so the fee buys you a full year if you return. Reconfirm fees on arrival — Lijiang's maintenance fee is applied inconsistently and some travellers report it isn't collected at the gates outside peak holidays.
